name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with only 22B engaged per token, cutting compute cost by 40% while matching or beating Llama-3.1-70B on benchmarks. The trade-off is higher memory pressure—you need 4x the VRAM of a dense 70B model—but the net capability gain per dollar spent outweighs the hardware bump.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B’s MoE routing overhead spikes EXCAVA’s latency at scale—its 22B engaged parameters still demand 4x VRAM, and the routing delay eats the compute savings. Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct’s flat 70B cost hides a real risk: its dense architecture avoids MoE’s latency spikes but locks you into a single model path. Test both under EXCAVA’s real load—if Qwen3’s 0.5% benchmark gain disappears in production, default to Llama-3.1-70B and optimize elsewhere.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its flat 70B architecture avoids MoE’s routing latency spikes, keeping response times predictable under load—critical for real-time tasks. The trade-off is higher per-token compute cost, but the stability and lower VRAM footprint outweigh the expense for EXCAVA’s current workload.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B’s MoE routing overhead isn’t the only latency killer—Llama-3.1-70B’s flat 70B dense mode still chokes on long-context tasks, where its memory-bound attention scales quadratically. A better alternative: test both models on EXCAVA’s worst-case prompt length with a 0.5% throughput bump as the tiebreaker—if neither clears it, default to the one with lower VRAM spikes.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour blind A/B stress test on EXCAVA’s 8xA100 node comparing Qwen3-235B-A22B vs Llama-3.1-70B on worst-case prompt length, measuring throughput delta ≥0.5%. Owner: Torque.
